purpose: reading-comprehension items; the contradicted item is composed by the pipeline from basis+alter and always shown with its label

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Recurrence-free survival for patients with undetectable ctDNA at diagnosis did not differ significantly between the NAC-treated and NAC-naïve cohorts.
statements.evidence: No statistically significant difference in recurrence-free survival for patients without detectable ctDNA at diagnosis was observed between the cohorts.
statements.note: The abstract reports no statistically significant difference in recurrence-free survival between the two cohorts for patients without detectable ctDNA at diagnosis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After radical cystectomy, ctDNA testing detected metastatic relapse in NAC-treated patients with 94% sensitivity and 98% specificity.
statements.evidence: Assessment of ctDNA after RC identified metastatic relapse with a sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 98% using the expanded follow-up data for the NAC-treated patients.
statements.note: The results give exactly these sensitivity and specificity values for post-cystectomy ctDNA in the NAC-treated cohort.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with detectable ctDNA at diagnosis who cleared it during NAC had outcomes similar to patients with undetectable ctDNA at diagnosis.
statements.evidence: ctDNA dynamics during NAC was independently associated with patient outcomes when adjusted for pathological downstaging (HR=4.7, p =0.029).
statements.note: The abstract says ctDNA dynamics during NAC predict outcome, but it never compares patients who cleared ctDNA with patients who were ctDNA-negative at diagnosis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumors shedding ctDNA at baseline were enriched for the Ba/Sq subtype and for epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle gene sets.
statements.evidence: Baseline ctDNA positivity was associated with the Ba/Sq subtype and enrichment of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle associated gene sets.
statements.note: The RNA-sequencing result links baseline ctDNA positivity to the Ba/Sq subtype and to EMT and cell-cycle gene set enrichment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In TCGA breast tumors, HOXB13 expression was significantly higher in HER2+ than HER2- cancers and in ER- than ER+ cancers.
statements.evidence: In the TCGA breast cancer cohort, HOXB13 gene expression was significantly higher in HER2+ versus HER2- breast cancers, and its expression was also significantly higher in the ER- versus ER+ breast cancers.
statements.note: The first result sentence reports both comparisons with HOXB13 higher in HER2+ and in ER- tumors.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with ERBB2/HOXB13 co-amplified, BRCA1-lost breast tumors respond better to PARP inhibitors than patients with ERBB2-only amplification.
statements.evidence: ERBB2/HOXB13 co-amp tumors with interstitial BRCA1 loss exhibit a mutational signature associated with APOBEC deaminase activity, and copy number signatures associated with chromothripsis and genomic instability.
statements.note: The abstract characterizes the genomic features and survival of these tumors but tests no therapy, so PARP inhibitor response is neither stated nor refuted.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across ERBB2-amplified tumors from different tissues, co-amplification of ERBB2/HOXB13 with BRCA1 loss was found only in breast cancer.
statements.evidence: Among ERBB2 -amplified tumors of different tissue origins, ERBB2/HOXB13 co-amp with a BRCA1 loss appeared to be unique to breast cancer.
statements.note: The abstract states that this co-amplification with BRCA1 loss appeared unique to breast cancer among ERBB2-amplified tumors of various origins.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Patients whose tumors had ERBB2/HOXB13 co-amplification with BRCA1 loss had significantly shorter PFS than patients with ERBB2-only amplification.
statements.evidence: patients with ERBB2/HOXB13 co-amplified and BRCA1 lost tumors displayed a significantly shorter progression-free survival (PFS) than those with ERBB2 -only amplifications.
statements.note: The abstract reports significantly shorter, not longer, progression-free survival for ERBB2/HOXB13 co-amplified, BRCA1-lost tumors compared with ERBB2-only amplification.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Cirsiliol reduced tumor growth in a mouse xenograft model of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
statements.evidence: The most promising candidate was subsequently validated in vitro using cytotoxicity assays (TU177 and RK33 cell lines) and wound healing migration assays, alongside MMP9 knockdown models to confirm mechanistic specificity.
statements.note: Validation was done only in cell lines; the abstract reports no animal experiment, so in vivo efficacy is neither shown nor ruled out.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among the screened phytochemicals, Cirsiliol showed the most favorable MMP9 binding free energy, -179.793 kJ/mol, with stable contacts to ALA189, HIS266 and LEU243.
statements.evidence: Virtual screening and MD simulations identified Cirsiliol as the most potent inhibitor among the tested phytochemicals, exhibiting a highly favorable binding free energy (ΔG binding = -179.793 kJ/mol) and stable interactions with key residues (ALA189, HIS266, and LEU243).
statements.note: The docking and MD results name Cirsiliol as the top candidate with this binding free energy and these residue interactions.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Cirsiliol inhibited growth of both laryngeal cancer cell lines dose-dependently, with a lower IC50 in RK33 cells than in TU177 cells.

alter.from: lower IC50 in RK33 cells than in TU177 cells
alter.to: lower IC50 in TU177 cells than in RK33 cells

statements.evidence: Cirsiliol induced dose-dependent growth inhibition with IC 50 values of 31.59 μM in TU177 cells and 17.73 μM in RK33 cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports IC50 values of 17.73 μM in RK33 cells and 31.59 μM in TU177 cells, so the lower IC50 was in RK33 cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cirsiliol significantly reduced cell migration, reproducing the effect seen in MMP9-knockdown TU177 cells.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, the compound significantly suppressed cell migration, mirroring the effects observed in MMP9-knockdown TU177 cells.
statements.note: The migration assay result states that Cirsiliol significantly suppressed migration, mirroring MMP9 knockdown.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the TDP-43 mice, RTE/ERV expression began with the onset of neurological phenotypes, appearing earlier in hTDP-43-Q331K than in hTDP-43-WT animals.
statements.evidence: Expression begins with onset of neurological phenotypes, earlier in hTDP-43-Q331K animals and later in hTDP-43-WT.
statements.note: The abstract ties expression onset to phenotype onset and states it is earlier in the Q331K mutant line than in the wild-type line.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: TDP-43 mice showed broad RTE/ERV expression with LINE-1 retrotransposition in both glia and neurons of the motor cortex.
statements.evidence: We found that TDP-43 animals exhibit broad expression of RTEs/ERVs with LINE-1 retrotransposition in glia and neurons in the motor cortex.
statements.note: The abstract reports LINE-1 retrotransposition in both glia and neurons of the motor cortex, not in glia alone.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Unlabeled cells died as a function of their distance from clusters of LINE-1-EGFP-labeled neurons and glia.
statements.evidence: Unlabeled cells also die as a function of distance from the clusters of LINE-1-EGFP labeled neurons and glial cells.
statements.note: The abstract states that death of unlabeled cells depends on distance from the labeled clusters.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Blocking reverse transcriptase pharmacologically prolonged the survival of the TDP-43 transgenic mice.
statements.evidence: Together, these findings support the hypothesis that TDP-43 pathology triggers RTE/ERV expression in the motor cortex, that such expression marks cells for programmed cell death, with cell non-autonomous effects on nearby neurons and glial cells.
statements.note: The mouse work is observational; no drug or other intervention against retrotransposition is reported, so this is neither supported nor refuted.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: SBS01 was significantly more frequent in White than in Asian gastric cancer cases (19.3% vs. 11.3%, P = 0.012).

alter.from: more frequent in White than in Asian
alter.to: more frequent in Asian than in White

statements.evidence: SBS01 and SBS20 showed significant differences between Whites vs. All Asians (19.3% vs. 11.3% for SBS 1 (P = 0.012) and 11.4% vs. 5.9% for SBS20 (P = 0.025), respectively)
statements.note: The abstract gives 19.3% in Whites versus 11.3% in Asians for SBS01, so the signature was more frequent in White cases.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Gastric cancer patients whose tumors carried SBS20 had worse survival than those whose tumors lacked it.
statements.evidence: Results hold promise for new insights in understanding risk and prognosis factors in GC.
statements.note: Prognosis is mentioned only as a future direction; no survival or outcome analysis for any signature is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Whole exome sequencing of 175 Chinese gastric cancer cases identified 104 mutated genes at P < 0.01, seven of which reached q < 0.0001.
statements.evidence: We identified 104 mutated genes with P < 0.01. Seven genes (OR6B1, B2M, ELF3, RHOA, RPL22, TP53, ARIDIA) had q < 0.0001, including six previously associated with GC.
statements.note: The results list 104 genes at P < 0.01 and seven at q < 0.0001 from the 175-case WES analysis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The commonest SBS signatures in the Chinese cases (SBS05, SBS01, SBS15, SBS20, SBS40) were also present in 254 White gastric cancer cases from TCGA.
statements.evidence: The most frequent SBS signatures (SBS05, SBS01, SBS15, SBS20, SBS40) were also observed in 254 White GC cases from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) Project.
statements.note: The abstract states that these five most frequent signatures were also observed in the 254 White TCGA cases.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SCARCE correctly identified true variants in a subpopulation of only 10 of 16,316 cells, 0.06% of all cells analyzed.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that SCARCE correctly isolates and identifies true variants in a cell population comprising just 10 of 16,316 cells (0.06% of the total population).
statements.note: The results give exactly these numbers for the smallest population in which SCARCE recovered true variants.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SCARCE recovered rare somatic mutations in three separate datasets, including MissionBio Tapestri data and clonally amplified single-cell whole-genome sequencing.
statements.evidence: SCARCE successfully identifies rare somatic mutations across three distinct datasets using technologies including MissionBio Tapestri and clonally-amplified whole-genome sequencing of single cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports successful identification across three distinct datasets generated with these technologies.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: SCARCE identified a causal somatic mutation in cells from a patient with an autoimmune disease.
statements.evidence: Somatic mutations are increasingly recognised as drivers of diseases beyond cancer, including autoimmune disorders.
statements.note: Autoimmune disease appears only as motivation in the background; the abstract does not say which diseases the three datasets came from.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: In an extensively characterized sample with known causal variants, SCARCE placed all known pathogenic variants among its top-ranked candidates.

alter.to: none of the known pathogenic variants

statements.evidence: in an extensively characterised sample with known causal variants, SCARCE correctly identifies all known pathogenic variants among its top-ranked candidates.
statements.note: The abstract reports that all known pathogenic variants in that sample were among SCARCE's top-ranked candidates.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients with a high CGPS gained more benefit from taxane chemotherapy than from androgen receptor pathway inhibitors.
statements.evidence: This interactive tool could support prospective plasma CNA-based risk stratification in mCRPC.
statements.note: The study builds prognostic survival models; it reports nothing about treatment choice or differential benefit by CGPS.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: The integrated clinico-genomic model had a higher C-index than either CGPS alone or clinical factors alone.
statements.evidence: C-index was 0.73 for the integrated model compared with 0.70 for CGPS alone and 0.63 for clinical factors alone.
statements.note: The abstract reports a C-index of 0.73 for the integrated model, above 0.70 for CGPS alone and 0.63 for clinical factors alone.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The integrated clinico-genomic model reached time-dependent AUCs of 0.79 at 24 months and 0.77 at 36 months, versus 0.65 and 0.71 for clinical factors alone.
statements.evidence: Time-dependent AUC values for the integrated clinico-genomic model at 24 and 36 months were 0.79 and 0.77, respectively, compared with 0.65 and 0.71 for using contemporary clinical factors alone
statements.note: These AUC values are reported directly in the results for the integrated model and for clinical factors alone.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CGPS estimates agreed closely across the independent cohorts, with Pearson correlation coefficients between 0.86 and 0.97.
statements.evidence: CGPS estimates across independent mCRPC cohorts showed high concordance with Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.86-0.97 for cross cohort comparisons.
statements.note: The abstract reports cross-cohort Pearson correlations of 0.86-0.97 for CGPS estimates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Alterations in TP53, RB1 or PTEN were associated with higher 18F-FDG avidity, larger metabolic tumor volume and worse prognosis.
statements.evidence: Genomic alterations in tumor suppressor genes TP53, RB1, or PTEN were associated with higher 18 F-FDG avidity and metabolic tumor volume on 18 F-FDG PET imaging and worse prognosis.
statements.note: The results sentence links these tumor suppressor alterations to higher FDG avidity, metabolic tumor volume and worse prognosis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The combination produced deeper responses than 177Lu-PSMA-617 given without pembrolizumab.
statements.evidence: The PRINCE trial showed the clinical activity for 177 Lu-PSMA-617 in combination with pembrolizumab for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
statements.note: All participants received the combination; the abstract makes no comparison with either agent alone.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Low baseline ctDNA fraction and high PSMA avidity in metastatic lesions were linked to superior treatment responses.
statements.evidence: A low baseline ctDNA fraction and high PSMA avidity in metastatic lesions were linked to superior treatment responses and may have composite biomarker value.
statements.note: The abstract links a low, not high, baseline ctDNA fraction together with high PSMA avidity to superior responses.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: At 12 weeks on treatment, both ctDNA detection and PSMA PET imaging were strong indicators of response depth and durability.
statements.evidence: At 12-wk on-treatment, both ctDNA detection and PSMA PET imaging were strong indicators of response depth and durability.
statements.note: The abstract states this for the 12-week on-treatment time point.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of 1122 retrieved publications, 807 were primary articles and 315 were review articles.
statements.evidence: A total of 1122 publications were retrieved: 807 primary articles and 315 review articles.
statements.note: The results give exactly these counts.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Annual publication volume rose significantly over 2012-2022, with a compound annual growth rate of 48.3%.
statements.evidence: The annual publication volume exhibited a significant upward trajectory, with a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 48.3%.
statements.note: The abstract reports a compound annual growth rate of 48.3% for annual publication volume.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Review articles accumulated more citations on average than primary research articles.
statements.evidence: A total of 1122 publications were retrieved: 807 primary articles and 315 review articles.
statements.note: The abstract counts primary and review articles but reports citations only by country and author, not by article type.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: China produced the most papers (379), but papers from the United States gathered the most citations (20,239).
statements.evidence: China had the highest article output (379 papers), whereas the citation rate of papers from the United States was the highest (20,239 citations).
statements.note: The abstract reports China as the top producer and the United States as the most cited country with these figures.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: High activity scores for the AR, FOXA1 and GRHL2 gene sets were significantly associated with poorer progression-free survival (P<0.05).
statements.evidence: we developed a gene set activity scoring algorithm and observed significant association of high activity scores with poor progression-free survival (P<0.05).
statements.note: The abstract reports that high activity scores were associated with poor, not better, progression-free survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: At baseline, 1,642 of 23,433 genes showed significant 5hmC differences between patients who did and did not progress (FDR<0.1).
statements.evidence: Differential methylation analysis in baseline samples identified significant 5hmC difference in 1,642 of 23,433 genes between patients with and without progression (false discovery rate, FDR<0.1).
statements.note: The results give exactly these gene counts and FDR threshold for the baseline comparison.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gene set activity scores fell significantly after 3 months of ADT (P<0.0001) and rose again at disease progression (P<0.05).
statements.evidence: Longitudinal analysis showed that the high activity scores were significantly reduced after 3-months of initiating ADT (P<0.0001) but returned to higher levels when the disease was progressed (P<0.05).
statements.note: The longitudinal result describes the drop at 3 months and the rebound at progression with these P values.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Adding an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor to ADT reversed the 5hmC hypermethylation of androgen-response gene sets.
statements.evidence: may be used as biomarkers to determine early treatment resistance, monitor disease progression, and potentially identify patients who would benefit from upfront treatment intensification.
statements.note: Treatment intensification is raised only as a possible future use; no intensified regimen was given or measured in this study.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nearly a third of TF-tissue pairs with enough mutations showed significant mutation enrichment at one or more binding-site positions.
statements.evidence: Nearly one third of pairs with sufficient mutation counts showed significant enrichment at one or more binding site positions.
statements.note: The abstract states that nearly one third of pairs with sufficient mutation counts showed significant enrichment.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Highly expressed TFs were more likely than lowly expressed TFs to show mutation enrichment at their binding sites.
statements.evidence: Highly expressed TFs were more likely to show enrichment than lowly expressed TFs, consistent with a role for TF binding in increased mutagenesis at the binding sites.
statements.note: The abstract reports that highly expressed TFs were more likely, not less likely, to show enrichment than lowly expressed TFs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutations enriched at TF binding sites changed the expression of the genes those TFs regulate.
statements.evidence: our study provides a roadmap for experimental assessment of TF-induced mutagenesis and informs the interpretation and prioritization of non-coding mutations in cancer.
statements.note: The catalog maps where mutations are enriched and which processes may cause them; it does not test whether the mutations alter target gene expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutation enrichment at TF binding sites was most widespread in melanoma but was found in every one of the 15 tissue types.
statements.evidence: Enrichment was most widespread in melanoma but was detected in all 15 tissue types, with the affected TFs and binding site positions varying across tissues.
statements.note: The abstract reports melanoma as the tissue with the most widespread enrichment and detection in all 15 tissue types.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: shearwater-AND detected ctDNA in most patients with stage I colorectal cancer.
statements.evidence: Our study benchmarked Mutect2, VarScan2, shearwater, and DREAMS-vc using deep targeted sequencing of cfDNA with Unique Molecular Identifiers (UMIs) from 111 colorectal cancer patients.
statements.note: The abstract gives no breakdown of the 111 patients by stage and no per-stage detection rate for any caller.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: shearwater-AND gave the highest precision for tumor-derived mutations and a ROC-AUC of 0.984 for sample classification in tumor-informed analyses.
statements.evidence: The shearwater-AND variant calling method demonstrated the highest precision in detecting tumor-derived mutations from plasma, and reached the highest ROC-AUC of 0.984 for sample classification in tumor-informed cfDNA analyses.
statements.note: The results report both the highest precision and the 0.984 ROC-AUC for shearwater-AND in the tumor-informed setting.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Differences in PBMC sequencing depth produced false positives, especially with VarScan2 and Mutect2, which downsampling to equal mean depth resolved.
statements.evidence: sequencing depth differences in PBMCs could lead to false positives, particularly with VarScan2 and Mutect2, which was addressed by downsampling to equivalent mean depths.
statements.note: The abstract reports this depth-related false positive problem and that downsampling addressed it.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: In tumor-agnostic analyses, DREAMS-vc had the best sample classification performance, with a ROC-AUC of 0.808.
statements.evidence: DREAMS-vc exhibited the highest ROC-AUC of 0.808 for sample classification in tumor-agnostic studies.
statements.note: The abstract attributes the highest tumor-agnostic ROC-AUC of 0.808 to DREAMS-vc, not VarScan2.
